answer_text:
Conjugation in \(S_n\) preserves cycle structure: if \(\tau\alpha\tau^{-1}=\gamma\), then \(\alpha\) and \(\gamma\) must have the same cycle lengths.

The cycle lengths of \(\alpha\) are:
\[
(1,2,4,8):\ 4,\qquad (3,5,7,9,11,13):\ 6,\qquad (6,12):\ 2,
\]
and the element \(10\) is fixed, so there is also a 1-cycle.

Thus \(\alpha\) has cycle type \((4,6,2,1)\).

The cycle lengths of \(\gamma\) are:
\[
(1,2,3,4):\ 4,\qquad (5,6,7,8,9,10,11):\ 7,\qquad (12,13):\ 2.
\]

Thus \(\gamma\) has cycle type \((4,7,2)\).

Since the cycle types are different, \(\alpha\) and \(\gamma\) are not conjugate in \(S_{13}\). Therefore there are no permutations \(\tau\) satisfying the equation.

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
